summary: Searches a linked list for an entry whose data word at +4 matches the global dword_8ACFCC. Reads the list header at this+0xC; when non-null, copies the head pointer into the header cursor slot (this+0x14) and walks the list. For each entry it compares the word at entry+4 against dword_8ACFCC; on mismatch it advances the cursor through the entry node next-pointer and continues; on match it clears the word at entry+0x18 (a match flag) and returns. Returns without modification when the header, the head pointer, or a cursor data pointer is null. Called by sub_4B3400.

local_names.v2: head pointer (first DWORD of the header)
local_names.v5: list header pointer reloaded inside the walk

operations.description: If the list header pointer this+0xC (this[3]) is null, skip the search entirely.
Copy the header head pointer (field *(this+0xC)+0) into the cursor slot this+0x14 so iteration starts at the head.
If the head pointer is null, skip the search because the cursor already equals the null head.
If the first entry data pointer (field of the cursor at +0) is null, return without modifying anything.
Walk entries while the word at current-entry+4 does not equal the comparison global dword_8ACFCC.
Advance the cursor: when the current cursor value is non-null, overwrite the cursor slot this+0x14 with the current cursor node's next-pointer (+4).
After advancing, if the new cursor is null, or its data pointer is null, stop iterating and return without a match.
On match (entry+4 equals dword_8ACFCC), when the entry data word at +4 is non-null, clear the entry match-flag word at +0x18 to 0.
The function returns void; control falls out after a found match, the null guards, or exhaustion of the walk.
Invoked by sub_4B3400 (004b3400) as the list-search utility.
